title: Proviral Hiding Places & Shedding Windows — Feline Leukemia p27 Antigen, FIV Maternal Antibodies & Canine Parvovirus SNAP Traps

teenKit.tldr: Medical tests that claim 99% accuracy can still trick you due to brutal math and sneaky hiding viruses. Understanding how hidden retroviruses and low disease rates shatter diagnostic certainties reveals how biology outsmarts our best technology.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Mastering how diagnostic tests fail protects you from falling into false traps when navigating medical decisions for yourself, your family, or your pets.
keyTakeaways: A "99% accurate" test does not mean a positive result guarantees a 99% chance of having the disease if the condition is actually rare.
Retroviruses like FeLV can go into deep undercover mode, hiding their DNA inside host cells or dodging detection systems entirely.
Kittens can test positive for viruses simply because they inherited protective antibodies from their mother, not because they are actively infected.

vocab.meaning: The mathematical probability that you actually have a disease when a medical test gives you a positive result.
Viral genetic material that has sneaked in and permanently stitched itself directly into the host's own cellular DNA.
Immune proteins passed from a mother to her baby that temporarily fight off infections but can accidentally trick diagnostic tests.
A narrow, specific timeframe when an infected body is actively releasing viral particles into the environment.

quiz.question: If a rare disease affects only 1 in 1,000 people, why might a positive result from a 99% accurate test still be a false alarm?
options: The test machine is always broken when it gets cold.
The sheer volume of healthy people taking the test means false positives can outnumber true positives.
Viruses mutate every time they touch a plastic cassette.
quiz.explanation: When a disease is rare, the massive pool of healthy people creates enough accidental false positives to overpower the true positive results.

quiz.question: What does a retrovirus like FeLV do during its regressive infection stage?
options: It hides its genetic code directly inside the host's bone marrow DNA where standard protein tests might miss it.
It instantly destroys all cells in the body within 24 hours.
It turns the host's fur completely neon green.
It refuses to replicate unless exposed to bright sunlight.
quiz.explanation: During the regressive stage, the virus integrates its proviral DNA silently into the host's cells, bypassing standard soluble antigen protein tests.

quiz.question: Why might a 4-week-old kitten test positive for an antibody-based virus test even if it is completely healthy?
options: The kitten manufactured the antibodies all by itself through intense exercise.
The kitten has permanent immunity that will never fade.
The kitten is carrying leftover maternal antibodies passed down from its mother.
The test is reacting to the kitten's food.
quiz.explanation: Antibodies from the mother circulate in a kitten's blood for weeks, frequently triggering antibody tests and mimicking an active infection.
